decisions.reason: The cover-letter page count, signature, and photo-relocation decision does not change any proposal-table requirement.
Moving favored photos to another section if needed does not necessarily change the proposal narrative, fixed section order, or unresolved Section 6 content.
The cross-Requirement photo-placement effect is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY at message 96; no addition or edit is needed.
The source changes the independently tracked cover-letter layout and photo placement, not the current full-document layout or special-page background treatment.
The client's hope of adding a signature smoothly in Canva does not change the existing Canva source platform, ownership, edit access, or asset policy.
The cover-letter revision does not change the final PDF format, file count, email submission method, or export requirements.
Adding the client's signature to the cover letter does not necessarily modify the Agua Arc brand identity or supplied brand assets.
The source decision has no effect on hyperlink functionality in the saved proposal.
The one-page constraint applies specifically to the cover letter and does not alter the separate whole-proposal page-limit state or reduction approach.
The source supplies revision content but does not change the number or trigger of the consolidated revision round.
The source concerns the separate GreenLatinos RFQ cover letter and has no effect on the TPEC proposal-design requirement.
The cover-letter revisions do not change any draft, revision, submission, or delivery deadline.
